name: Montclair
intro: Montclair pairs a lively arts scene with steady support for older residents. The township's Senior Services office, known as Lifelong Montclair, runs classes in health, art and wellness from Edgemont Park House. The Montclair Art Museum and the Presby Memorial Iris Gardens are close by, and the library delivers books to residents who can't get out.

seniorCenter.name: Senior Services / Lifelong Montclair
seniorCenter.address: Edgemont Park House, 290 Valley Road, Montclair, NJ 07042
seniorCenter.notes: Events and classes in health, education, art, recreation and wellness, held at Edgemont Park House and other spots around town. Register online through the township's class portal, or call 973-744-3278 if you don't use a computer.

transport.name: Essex County Community Transportation
transport.notes: Free rides for people 60 and over or with a disability to medical visits, shopping and programs within Essex County. New riders give their details by phone first. Book Monday to Friday, 9 am to 3 pm, at least two days and up to a month ahead.

library.name: Montclair Public Library
library.notes: Home Assisted Services brings books, audiobooks, DVDs and hotspots to Montclair residents who can't easily leave home (ext. 2232). The library also has assistive technology such as a text magnifier, one-on-one tech help by appointment, and Medicare counseling referrals through the Reference Desk (ext. 2235).

more.name: Montclair Public Health Nursing
more.note: Nursing services from the township Health Department, free or for a small fee. Municipal Building, 205 Claremont Avenue, third floor.

more.name: The MILL (Montclair Institute for Lifelong Learning)
more.note: Free classes for adults 55 and over at spots around town. Registration is required.

places.name: Montclair Art Museum
places.note: At 3 South Mountain Avenue, with gallery hours Friday to Sunday, a senior ticket price and free parking onsite.

places.name: Presby Memorial Iris Gardens
places.note: County garden at 474 Upper Mountain Avenue with about 3,000 iris varieties. Peak bloom is usually mid May to early June.

places.name: Eagle Rock Reservation
places.note: County woodland on the ridge between West Orange, Montclair and Verona, with scenic overlooks and a September 11 memorial.

sources: Seniors, People with Disabilities Transportation (Township of Montclair)
Register for Classes and Programs (Township of Montclair)
Presby Memorial Iris Gardens (Essex County Parks)

name: West Orange
intro: West Orange's Department of Senior Services runs free and low-cost classes at spots around town, from the Katz Community Center to the public library, plus sessions on Zoom. The township also gives curb-to-curb rides to residents 60 and over. Thomas Edison's laboratory and Glenmont estate are here, along with Turtle Back Zoo.

seniorCenter.name: West Orange Department of Senior Services
seniorCenter.address: 66 Main Street, Room 207, West Orange, NJ 07052
seniorCenter.notes: Classes and events at the Katz Community Center, Ginny Duenkel Pool, the public library, O'Connor Park and on Zoom, offered free or at a low cost. Call to register or to join the email list.

transport.name: West Orange Senior Citizen Transportation Program
transport.notes: Curb-to-curb rides within West Orange for residents 60 and over. Medical trips come first, then the library, shopping, club meetings and the food pantry. Riders must meet the bus at the curb or bring an aide, and a lift bus serves wheelchair users. Call 2 to 3 days ahead.

library.name: West Orange Public Library
library.notes: Free homebound delivery every Friday to homes, apartments and senior residences. Call 973-736-0198 to sign up. Reference librarians can help with basic computer questions at 973-736-0196.

more.name: Aging Well West Orange (Senior Livability)
more.note: The township's senior livability office, at 10 Gaston Street (rear).

more.name: West Orange Health Center
more.note: Township health center at 10 Gaston Street (rear).

places.name: Thomas Edison National Historical Park
places.note: Edison's laboratory complex at 211 Main Street. Glenmont estate tours are seasonal and involve many stairs.

places.name: Turtle Back Zoo
places.note: Essex County's zoo, with more than 200 species, at the South Mountain Recreation Complex.

places.name: South Mountain Reservation
places.note: About 2,110 acres of county woods with trails, carriage roads and a scenic overlook.

sources: Older Adult Resources (Township of West Orange)
Senior Citizen Transportation Program (Township of West Orange)
West Orange Public Library home page
Plan Your Visit (Thomas Edison National Historical Park)

name: Livingston
intro: Livingston's Senior/Community Center on Hillside Avenue is the hub for older residents, with talks, crafts, blood pressure checks and free tech help from high school students. A wheelchair-accessible township bus takes residents 62 and up around town. Riker Hill Art Park and the walking track at Memorial Oval make easy outings.

seniorCenter.name: Livingston Senior/Community Center (LSCC)
seniorCenter.notes: Home of Recreation and Senior Services and the Health Department. Programs include coffee talks, crafts, free blood pressure screenings and Keeping Up with Technology. Office hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

transport.name: Livingston Senior Transportation Program
transport.notes: For residents 62 and over and disabled residents 18 and over. A wheelchair-accessible bus runs weekdays, 8:45 am to 3 pm, to any Livingston location (ShopRite, the library, the YMCA) and to the JCC in West Orange. Book one week to 24 hours ahead; press option 1.

library.name: Livingston Public Library
library.address: 10 Robert H. Harp Drive, Livingston, NJ 07039
library.notes: Books by Mail sends Livingston books and DVDs to cardholders who can't visit, for a short time or for good, with return postage included. Apply online or on a paper form.

more.name: Keeping Up with Technology (ages 62+)
more.note: Free help with phones and tablets from Livingston High School students, twice a month at the center. Bring your own device and preregister.

more.name: Essex County Special Transportation System
more.note: County rides to medical appointments, dialysis, nutrition sites, food shopping and social activities.

places.name: Riker Hill Art Park
places.note: A former missile tracking base now home to dozens of artist studios. The county holds open houses, so check the county parks site for dates.

places.name: Memorial Oval and Park
places.note: Across from Town Hall, with a walking track, gazebo, bocce, shuffleboard and Littell's Pond.

sources: Keeping Up with Technology (Township of Livingston)
Memorial Oval and Park (Township of Livingston)
Riker Hill Art Park (Essex County Parks)

name: Verona
intro: Verona's Community Center on Bloomfield Avenue is home base for senior services, with a free senior bus, chair yoga and seated exercise classes. The Senior Club meets twice a month for speakers, bingo and cake. Verona Park's lake and walking paths and the trails of Hilltop Reservation are both close to home.

seniorCenter.name: Verona Community Center (Senior Services)
seniorCenter.notes: Weekday office for senior services and exercise sign-ups. The Senior Club meets in the ballroom at 1 pm on the first and third Wednesdays, September to June, with dues of $10 a year, free bus rides to meetings, parties and trips.

transport.name: Verona Senior Bus
transport.notes: Free, for Verona residents only, with pick-up at home. A 9 am local run stops along Bloomfield Avenue and a 10 am run goes to grocery stores on the monthly calendar. Call at 8:30 am on the day you want to ride; seats are limited.

library.name: Verona Public Library
library.notes: Regular hours include Sundays, noon to 5 pm. Summer hours are shorter.

more.name: Medical Transport for Verona and Cedar Grove Seniors
more.note: Rides to medical appointments in nearby towns, including Mountainside and Saint Barnabas hospitals. $5 within Verona and Cedar Grove, $10 elsewhere. Book 1 to 2 weeks ahead, weekdays 10 am to noon. Riders must get in and out of the vehicle on their own.

more.name: Adult/Senior Exercise Classes
more.note: Chair-based strength classes and chair yoga with certified instructors. Register online through Community Pass or at the Community Center.

places.name: Verona Park
places.note: 54-acre county park with a 13-acre lake, walking paths, a gazebo and boat rentals in season.

places.name: Hilltop Reservation
places.note: County nature preserve on the Second Watchung Mountain with short ridge trails, entered at 255 Fairview Avenue in Verona.

places.name: Eagle Rock Reservation
places.note: County woodland on the ridge between West Orange, Montclair and Verona, with scenic overlooks and a September 11 memorial.

sources: Verona Senior Citizen Bus (Township of Verona)

name: Glen Ridge
intro: Glen Ridge keeps its senior programs small and friendly, based at the restored 1887 train station on Ridgewood Avenue. There are monthly luncheons with blood pressure checks, chair yoga and art classes, and a jitney for grocery runs. The library delivers books through volunteers, and Freeman Gardens is a pretty spot for a walk.

seniorCenter.name: Glen Ridge Senior/Community Center (Train Station)
seniorCenter.notes: Programs for Glen Ridge seniors, including a monthly luncheon with a blood pressure screening, chair yoga on Zoom, art classes at the train station, and field trips. Sign up through the Recreation Office.

transport.name: Glen Ridge Senior Jitney
transport.notes: Jitney rides for a weekly ShopRite trip and for the monthly luncheon. Call the Recreation Office to reserve; space is limited.

library.name: Glen Ridge Public Library
library.notes: Volunteers deliver up to 10 items once or twice a month to residents who can't visit because of illness or limited mobility. It starts with a short phone interview.

more.name: Senior Activities Calendar
more.note: Monthly calendar of senior programs. Sign up by phone or in person at the train station.

places.name: Freeman Gardens
places.note: Volunteer-run rose garden at Maolis and Hawthorne Avenues.

places.name: The Glen bike path and gazebo
places.note: Path along the south side of Bloomfield Avenue between Hillside Avenue and Freeman Parkway.

sources: Senior Citizen Programs (Borough of Glen Ridge)
Senior Activities Calendar (Borough of Glen Ridge)

name: Bloomfield
intro: Bloomfield has social workers on staff to help older residents with Medicare, food, housing and utility programs. Oakeside Seniors brings lunch, chair yoga, crafts and bingo to an 1895 mansion on Belleville Avenue. Free Dial-A-Ride trips go anywhere in Essex County, and Brookdale Park has a rose garden and a fitness path.

seniorCenter.name: Oakeside Seniors at Oakeside Cultural Center
seniorCenter.notes: The township's senior program meets Monday and Wednesday afternoons, with lunch, chair yoga, arts and crafts and bingo, and no registration needed. Run by the Division of Human Services, which posts a monthly senior calendar.

transport.name: Bloomfield Dial-A-Ride
transport.notes: Free curb-to-curb rides anywhere in Essex County for residents 60 and over or with a disability, mostly medical trips but also shopping, haircuts and visits. First come, first served. A free fixed-route Senior Citizen Bus also runs to stores, banks and Town Hall.

library.name: Bloomfield Public Library
library.notes: Metered parking behind the main library off State Street. Open Monday to Saturday.

more.name: Bloomfield Division of Human Services
more.note: Social workers screen seniors for programs such as Medicare savings, SNAP, utility help and the senior tax freeze, and help with the applications.

more.name: Bloomfield Senior Organization Club
more.note: Monthly meetings, holiday gatherings, speakers and trips. Dues are $20 a year.

places.name: Brookdale Park
places.note: County park off Watchung Avenue with a formal rose garden, walking trails and a 1.5 mile fitness course.

places.name: Watsessing Park
places.note: Olmsted-designed county park at Bloomfield Avenue and Conger Street, with a bandstand and a senior citizens building.

places.name: Oakeside Cultural Center
places.note: Historic 1895 estate with four acres of lawns and gardens.

sources: Senior Services and Programs (Township of Bloomfield)
Bloomfield Senior Citizen Bus (Township of Bloomfield)
Project Healthy Bones at Oakeside (Township of Bloomfield)
Oakeside senior programming (Township of Bloomfield on Facebook)

name: Nutley
intro: Nutley runs a full calendar for seniors through its Parks and Recreation department, including chair yoga, two senior clubs and a weekday nutrition lunch, with free transportation to most programs. A daily check-in call program adds peace of mind for people who live alone. Yanticaw Park and the Nutley Museum are easy outings.

seniorCenter.name: Nutley Senior Citizen and Recreation Center
seniorCenter.notes: The Senior Club meets Wednesdays at 12:30 pm, September to June, and the Old Guard Club meets Fridays at 9 am. Chair yoga is held at the Annex Building, and there is a May Day lunch and a September picnic. Call the Senior Citizen Coordinator for the full list.

transport.name: Nutley Senior Transportation
transport.notes: Free rides to most senior programs and the weekday nutrition lunch. ShopRite trips run Tuesdays and Fridays with a three-bag limit; homeowners call the office to set up a home pick-up.

library.name: Nutley Public Library
library.notes: Free ebooks, audiobooks and streaming with a library card through Libby, Hoopla and Kanopy.

more.name: Senior Nutrition Program
more.note: Weekday lunch, 11:30 am to 12:30 pm, at the Annex Building, 65 Bloomfield Avenue. Call Chrill Care (ext. 244) at least one day ahead.

more.name: Operation Reassurance
more.note: Free daily check-in call for seniors and disabled residents who live alone. If you don't call in between 8:30 and 10:30 am, the township calls you, then sends police or fire to check.

places.name: Yanticaw Park
places.note: County park between Centre Street and Chestnut Street, running west to Passaic Avenue.

places.name: Nutley Museum
places.note: Restored 1875 Church Street School at 65 Church Street, with local history exhibits and Annie Oakley memorabilia.

sources: Senior Citizen Programs and Activities (Township of Nutley)
Essex County Senior Centers (Essex County WeCare)

name: Maplewood
intro: Maplewood's Senior Center on Burnett Avenue runs programs for adults 55 and over, and the township's Dial-A-Ride bus handles short local trips. A Jewish Family Services social worker shared with South Orange is available on Wednesdays. South Mountain Reservation and the historic Durand-Hedden House are close to home.

seniorCenter.name: Maplewood Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: Programs for adults 55 and over from the Department of Community Services, including fitness classes and social programs. Register online through Rec Desk or call the Community Services Desk at 973-762-8120.

transport.name: Maplewood Senior Bus (Dial-A-Ride)
transport.notes: Wheelchair-accessible bus for personal appointments up to a 15-minute ride away. Call at least 24 hours ahead and mention if you need wheelchair help.

library.name: Maplewood Memorial Library
library.notes: Recently renovated and expanded, and open seven days. The Hilton Branch at 1688 Springfield Avenue is a second option.

more.name: Older Adult Social Worker (Jewish Family Services)
more.note: A Jewish Family Services social worker shared by Maplewood and South Orange, available Wednesdays, 9 am to 3 pm. Call 973-986-4321 or email SomaSocialworker@southorange.org.

more.name: Maplewood Adult Health Clinics
more.note: Free for Maplewood residents 18 and over: blood pressure checks, medication counseling, lab work and more. Ask for ext. 4300.

more.name: SOMA Two Towns for All Ages
more.note: Aging-in-place initiative shared with South Orange, with a weekly email and an events calendar.

places.name: South Mountain Reservation
places.note: About 2,110 acres of county woods with trails, carriage roads and a scenic overlook.

places.name: Durand-Hedden House and Garden
places.note: Township-owned historic house at 523 Ridgewood Road, open about once a month from September to June, with talks and seasonal events.

sources: SOMA Two Towns for All Ages

name: South Orange
intro: South Orange shares its aging-in-place effort with Maplewood through SOMA Two Towns for All Ages, which shares news and events for older residents. A Jewish Family Services social worker is available on Wednesdays. The library is open in two temporary spots during its rebuild, and SOPAC is right in the village.

seniorCenter.name: SOMA Two Towns for All Ages (The Baird Center)
seniorCenter.notes: An aging-in-place initiative of South Orange and Maplewood rather than a drop-in senior center. It sends a weekly email and posts events for older residents and caregivers.

transport.name: South Orange Senior Bus (Dial-a-Ride)
transport.notes: Run by the South Orange Parking Authority. Call to check the current days and to book a ride.

library.name: South Orange Public Library
library.notes: The main building is under construction. Services continue at 298 Walton Avenue and at a branch in the Baird Center, 5 Mead Street, which has Sunday afternoon hours.

more.name: Older Adult Social Worker (Jewish Family Services)
more.note: A Jewish Family Services social worker shared by South Orange and Maplewood, available Wednesdays, 9 am to 3 pm, for help finding home care, meals, housing, Medicare counseling and transportation.

more.name: JFS Care Consultation Program
more.note: For family members caring for an older adult.

places.name: South Orange Performing Arts Center (SOPAC)
places.note: Theater in the center of the village with concerts, films and talks, close to restaurants and transit.

places.name: South Mountain Reservation
places.note: About 2,110 acres of county woods with trails, carriage roads and a scenic overlook.

sources: SOMA Two Towns for All Ages
Jitney Bus and Parking Authority (South Orange Village)

name: Millburn and Short Hills
intro: Millburn and Short Hills have a Senior Citizens Department that puts out the Senior Happenings e-newsletter and a monthly program calendar, with classes such as chair yoga and line dancing at the Bauer Community Center. A free senior bus runs four days a week. Greenwood Gardens and the Cora Hartshorn Arboretum offer quiet walks close by.

seniorCenter.name: Millburn Senior Citizens Department
seniorCenter.notes: Office hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. Leave your name and number for the Senior Citizen Coordinator. Many programs, such as chair yoga, line dancing and Friday Friends, meet at the Bauer Community Center at Taylor Park, 100 Main Street. Project Healthy Bones has a waiting list.

transport.name: Millburn Senior Bus
transport.notes: Free for residents 62 and over, within the township, to medical visits, shopping, the library and activities on Mondays, Wednesdays, Thursdays and Fridays. Call 7 to 8:15 am at least a day ahead; there is no voicemail. Regular shopping trips go to the Short Hills Mall (first Friday and third Wednesday of the month) and to Whole Foods/Target (last Wednesday).

library.name: Millburn Free Public Library
library.notes: You can text a librarian at 973-988-4228 or use the chat on the website.

more.name: EZ Ride Ryde4Life
more.note: Rides for older adults and people with reduced mobility. Choose option 4.

more.name: NJ Transit Access Link
more.note: Door-to-door rides across New Jersey for people who can't use the regular bus. Apply for eligibility first (option 1); a fee applies.

places.name: Greenwood Gardens
places.note: 28-acre public garden at 274 Old Short Hills Road, open seasonally with a lower senior ticket price. Check the garden's site for days and hours.

places.name: Cora Hartshorn Arboretum and Bird Sanctuary
places.note: About 16 acres of woodland with three miles of trails in Short Hills.

places.name: South Mountain Reservation
places.note: About 2,110 acres of county woods with trails, carriage roads and a scenic overlook.

name: Caldwell
intro: Caldwell's Grover Cleveland Senior Center welcomes anyone 60 and over for fitness, talks and social events, and a shared senior bus serves Caldwell, West Caldwell and Roseland. The borough's new library opened in June 2026 at 80 Bloomfield Avenue. The birthplace of President Grover Cleveland is on the same avenue, at number 207.

seniorCenter.name: Grover Cleveland Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: Open to anyone 60 and over, with fitness, enrichment, health talks and social events. It is part of the borough's Health and Human Services Department, and a monthly newsletter and calendar come by mail or email.

transport.name: Caldwell, West Caldwell and Roseland Senior Transportation
transport.notes: Curb-to-curb rides for residents of the three towns for food shopping, banks and pharmacies, plus a Tuesday trip to local malls. Call between 8:15 and 8:45 am on the day you want to ride.

library.name: Caldwell Public Library
library.notes: The new building opened June 29, 2026, with an automatic front door, its own parking lot and more public computers.

more.name: Caldwell Food Pantry
more.note: For Caldwell and West Caldwell residents, Wednesdays 11 am to 1 pm and Thursdays 4 to 6 pm. Call to confirm hours and location.

places.name: Grover Cleveland Birthplace
places.note: At 207 Bloomfield Avenue. The Presidential Library and Museum is open Wednesdays and Sundays, noon to 3 pm.

places.name: Grover Cleveland Park
places.note: 41-acre Olmsted-designed county park on the Caldwell and Essex Fells line, with walkways and a picnic grove.

sources: Health and Human Services Department (Borough of Caldwell)
Essex County Senior Centers (Essex County WeCare)

name: Cedar Grove
intro: Cedar Grove's Recreation Department plans senior exercise classes, luncheons and other programs, and a township bus makes weekly runs to markets, malls and banks. Seniors can also book medical rides through a program shared with Verona. Mills Reservation and Hilltop Reservation give the township wooded trails, including an overlook with a view of the New York skyline.

seniorCenter.name: Cedar Grove Recreation Department (Senior Programs)
seniorCenter.notes: Senior exercise sessions and a holiday luncheon are posted on the township's Senior Citizens page. Register online or call ext. 220.

transport.name: Cedar Grove Senior Bus
transport.notes: For seniors and residents with disabilities. Tuesdays go to the Route 46 Farmers Market and Little Falls ShopRite, Wednesdays to Willowbrook Mall and Kohl's, and Thursdays to local stores and banks. Pick-up is 9:15 am; call ext. 0 between 8:30 and 9 am that morning.

library.name: Cedar Grove Public Library
library.notes: Open Monday to Saturday, with evening hours Monday, Tuesday and Thursday. Closed Saturdays in July and August.

more.name: Medical Transport for Verona and Cedar Grove Seniors
more.note: Run through Verona. Rides to medical appointments in nearby towns, including Mountainside and Saint Barnabas hospitals, for $5 or $10. Book 1 to 2 weeks ahead, weekdays 10 am to noon.

places.name: Mills Reservation
places.note: 157 acres of county woods with walking trails and a cliff overlook toward the New York skyline.

places.name: Hilltop Reservation
places.note: County nature preserve on the Second Watchung Mountain with short ridge trails, entered at 255 Fairview Avenue in Verona.

name: Clifton
intro: Clifton's Senior Center sits on the City Hall grounds at 900 Clifton Avenue, where the city helps older residents with benefit forms, heating and cooling grants and Medicare counseling. A weekday senior lunch and outreach rides are offered, and the Clifton Arts Center's sculpture park is on the same campus.

seniorCenter.name: Clifton Senior Center
seniorCenter.address: 900 Clifton Avenue, Barn C-5, Clifton, NJ 07013
seniorCenter.notes: Home of the Office of Senior Citizen and Disabled Services, which helps with medical and tax forms, heating and cooling grants and Medicare counseling, with home visits when needed. Use the Colfax Avenue entrance.

transport.name: Clifton Outreach Transportation
transport.notes: For seniors and disabled adults with no other way to get around, Monday to Friday, to medical appointments, food shopping and the senior nutrition program. Call for an appointment.

library.name: Clifton Public Library (Main Memorial Library)
library.notes: Free monthly delivery of books, large print and audiobooks for residents who are homebound or live in a nursing home or assisted living. The Allwood Branch is at 44 Lyall Road, 973-471-0555.

more.name: Senior Nutrition Program
more.note: Lunch for seniors and disabled adults at the Senior Center, provided through the Passaic County Division on Aging.

more.name: Passaic County MOVE
more.note: App or phone booked shared rides in Passaic, Clifton and Paterson for $1.90 a ride (card only), weekdays 6 am to 8 pm. Pickup is at a nearby corner, and wheelchair accessible vehicles can be requested.

places.name: Clifton Arts Center and Sculpture Park
places.note: Gallery in two historic barns at the municipal complex, with more than 30 outdoor sculptures on the grounds.

places.name: Garret Mountain Reservation
places.note: Passaic County park in neighboring Woodland Park with a 5K loop, scenic overlooks and picnic areas.

name: Little Falls
intro: Little Falls has a Senior Services Coordinator and two senior clubs, the Jolly Seniors and the Golden Agers, based at the Civic Center on Warren Street. A township bus serves residents 55 and over. The library delivers to people who can't get out, and a Sunday farmers market runs behind Town Hall from May through October.

seniorCenter.name: Little Falls Civic Center (Senior Clubs)
seniorCenter.notes: The Jolly Seniors and Golden Agers clubs meet here, and the senior bus runs to club meetings on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Contact Senior Services Coordinator John Pace.

transport.name: Little Falls Senior Bus
transport.notes: For residents 55 and over, and disabled residents who can board on their own, to appointments and shopping in Little Falls, Woodland Park and Totowa, with daily ShopRite trips. Apply first for a pass at the Clerk's Office, 225 Main Street. No service on Wednesdays.

library.name: Little Falls Public Library
library.notes: Home delivery for Little Falls residents who can't get to the library. Call by 4 pm Friday for delivery the next Monday.

more.name: Little Falls Farmers Market
more.note: Sundays, 9 am to 2 pm, May through October, behind Town Hall at 225 Main Street.

places.name: Yogi Berra Museum and Learning Center
places.note: On the Montclair State campus at 8 Yogi Berra Drive, open Wednesday to Sunday, noon to 5 pm, with a senior ticket price and free wheelchairs.

places.name: Morris Canal Greenway
places.note: Passaic County walking and biking path along the route of the old canal, which ran through Little Falls.

sources: Senior Citizen Resources (Township of Little Falls)
Little Falls Senior Clubs (Township of Little Falls)
Senior Bus Service (Township of Little Falls)
Little Falls Farmers Market (Township of Little Falls)
Home Delivery Service (Little Falls Public Library)

name: Belleville
intro: Belleville's Senior Recreation Center on Franklin Avenue is open to residents 50 and older who sign up for a yearly Senior Pass, with bingo, crafts, bocce, exercise classes and trips. The township's Dial-A-Ride van takes residents 60 and older to local medical visits, supermarkets and the center on weekday mornings and early afternoons.

seniorCenter.name: Belleville Senior Recreation Center
seniorCenter.notes: Belleville residents 50 and older register for the Senior Pass, which gives full access to the center. Since January 1, an active pass is needed to enter. The pass costs $25 a year for residents and $50 for non-residents. Expect weekly bingo, arts and crafts, a pool table, a bocce court, exercise and wellness classes, socials and trips. Enrollment questions go to gpolite@bellevillenj.org.

transport.name: Belleville Dial-A-Ride
transport.notes: For Belleville residents 60 and older and adults 18 and older with disabilities who have registered with the service. Rides go to medical appointments in Belleville, Bloomfield and Nutley (Mountainside for dialysis only), to supermarkets, and to the Senior Recreation Center. Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m., with the last pickup call at 1:45 p.m. Book 24 hours ahead. Two bag limit on the shopping bus.

more.name: Essex County Office of Senior Services (ADRC)
more.note: The county's information line for older adults and caregivers, including respite care, home delivered meals and friendly visiting.

more.name: Essex County Special Transportation
more.note: County rides for older and disabled adults to medical and therapy visits. Book at least two business days ahead.

places.name: Belleville Park
places.note: A 32 acre county park along the Second River that continues Branch Brook Park's cherry blossoms, with a quarter mile path, bocce courts and a senior center.

places.name: Branch Brook Park
places.note: The nation's first county park, partly in Belleville, known for its cherry trees and annual Cherry Blossom Festival. The county runs a weekday senior lunch cafe here.

sources: Essex County Office of Senior Services

name: East Orange
intro: East Orange's Division of Senior Services, based at the senior center on Halsted Street, serves residents 60 and older and adults with disabilities. It offers weekly bowling, line dancing, exercise and craft classes, a monthly low-cost food co-op, help with benefit applications, and rides to doctors, banks, grocery stores and the library.

seniorCenter.name: East Orange Senior Center (Division of Senior Services)
seniorCenter.notes: For East Orange residents 60 and older and disabled adults. Weekly arts and crafts, bowling, exercise, line dancing and other activities, plus trips and an annual Senior Citizen Conference. Staff help with benefit applications and pre-screen for SNAP, energy assistance and prescription help. Low-cost ID cards, free File of Life cards, and light housekeeping help for those who need it.

transport.name: East Orange Senior Services transportation
transport.notes: The Division of Senior Services drives seniors and disabled adults to banks, benefit offices, grocery stores, the library, medical appointments, and recreational and cultural events. Call the division to register and arrange rides.

library.name: East Orange Public Library
library.address: 21 South Arlington Avenue, East Orange, NJ 07018

more.name: East Orange monthly Food Co-op
more.note: A low-cost monthly food co-op for seniors and disabled adults, run by the Division of Senior Services.

more.name: Essex County Office of Senior Services (ADRC)
more.note: The county's information line for older adults and caregivers, including respite care, home delivered meals and friendly visiting.

more.name: Essex County Special Transportation
more.note: County rides for older and disabled adults to medical and therapy visits. Book at least two business days ahead.

places.name: Watsessing Park
places.note: A 69 acre Olmsted designed county park shared with Bloomfield, with a bandstand and a senior citizens building. The county runs a weekday senior lunch cafe here.

places.name: Branch Brook Park
places.note: A short drive away in Newark, the nation's first county park is famous for its cherry blossoms and has a jogging loop and bocce courts.

sources: Essex County Office of Senior Services

name: Essex Fells
intro: Essex Fells has Grover Cleveland Park, the first county park in western Essex, inside its borders. The borough shares a health department with Livingston. For programs, the Grover Cleveland Senior Center in neighboring Caldwell welcomes anyone 60 and older, and the county runs rides to medical visits.

seniorCenter.name: Grover Cleveland Senior Center (Caldwell)
seniorCenter.notes: Essex Fells does not post its own senior program. This nearby center is run by the Borough of Caldwell in the Irene Gibbons Health & Human Services Building, and anyone 60 or older can take part in its fitness, enrichment, health education and social programs. Call for a monthly calendar.

transport.name: Essex County Special Transportation
transport.notes: Run for the county by Transdev for older adults and adults with disabilities. Rides go to non-emergency medical and therapy appointments, and the county also lists mall shopping and group trips. Book at least two business days ahead. Drivers give arm assistance but cannot help with stairs, and vehicles are wheelchair equipped.

more.name: Essex Fells Borough Hall
more.note: 255 Roseland Avenue. The borough posts Essex County senior events, such as the yearly Legacies writing contest.

more.name: Essex County Office of Senior Services
more.note: The county's information line for older adults and caregivers, including respite care, home delivered meals and friendly visiting.

more.note: Help with benefits, home care referrals, caregiver programs and the county's senior lunch sites (suggested donation $1.75; reserve two days ahead).

more.name: Union County Paratransit
more.note: Curb to curb rides for residents 60 and older anywhere in Union County, $3 each way. Reservations are taken weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

places.name: Watchung Reservation
places.note: A 2,065 acre county preserve nearby with lakes, woods, nature trails and the Trailside Nature and Science Center.

places.name: Passaic River Parkway
places.note: A county riverside park in Berkeley Heights, New Providence and Summit with nature trails and fishing.

name: Hackensack
intro: Hackensack is the Bergen County seat, so the county's senior services office is right in town at One Bergen County Plaza. The county also runs the United Senior Activity Center on Hudson Street, where residents 60 and over can join free, eat a weekday lunch and take classes from line dancing to yoga.

seniorCenter.name: United Senior Activity Center
seniorCenter.notes: Run by Bergen County. Free for Bergen County residents 60 and over. Open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Lunch is served daily at 11:30 a.m. for a suggested $1.25 donation; reserve by 11:30 a.m. the day before. Regular activities include morning music, bingo, exercise, Zumba, yoga, line dancing and ESL classes.

transport.name: Bergen County Division of Community Transportation
transport.notes: Rides for seniors, frail residents and people with disabilities who live in Bergen County, for trips such as routine medical visits, physical therapy, shopping and senior activity centers. Call and press 1 for dispatch.

library.name: Johnson Public Library
library.notes: Offers Tech Help sessions for adults and a Books by Mail service. Open Monday to Thursday 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., Friday and Saturday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.

more.name: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Senior Center
more.note: 375 First Street. Free programs for adults 60 and over, open weekdays 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., funded through the Bergen County Division of Senior Services.

more.name: Bergen County Division of Senior Services
more.note: The county helpline for information, care management, Medicare counseling (SHIP) and meals. Toll free 1-877-222-3737.

places.name: Borg's Woods Nature Preserve
places.note: About 15 acres of quiet forest with simple walking trails. There is no formal parking lot.

places.name: Hackensack River County Park
places.note: A Bergen County park in Hackensack. The county parks office at 201-336-7275 can tell you what is there.

name: Paramus
intro: Paramus gives residents 62 and over a free senior center on North Farview Avenue with a full weekday schedule, from chair yoga and bocce to mahjong and casino trips. The borough also runs a free senior bus for shopping, club meetings and Sunday Mass, and Van Saun County Park charges county seniors just $2 at its zoo.

seniorCenter.name: Joseph Cipolla Senior Activity Center
seniorCenter.notes: Ask for extension 6200. For Paramus residents 62 and over, with no fee to join. Center hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Activities include art, billiards, bingo, bocce, book club, chair yoga, knitting, line dancing, mahjong, ping pong and yoga.

transport.name: Paramus Senior Bus
transport.notes: Free for senior citizens who live in Paramus. Runs a set schedule Monday through Friday to local malls, shopping centers, grocery stores and the senior center, and to Our Lady of Visitation for Sunday Mass. No service on borough holidays or in bad weather. Scheduling goes through the Department of Public Works.

library.name: Paramus Public Library
library.notes: The Charles E. Reid Branch is at 239 West Midland Avenue (201-444-4911). Both offer adult programs, museum passes and eBooks and audiobooks.

more.name: Bergen County Division of Senior Services
more.note: The county helpline for information, care management, Medicare counseling (SHIP) and meals. Toll free 1-877-222-3737.

more.name: Bergen County Division of Community Transportation
more.note: County rides for seniors and people with disabilities, including routine medical visits. Press 1 for dispatch.

places.name: Van Saun County Park and Bergen County Zoo
places.note: The zoo is open daily from 10 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Bergen County seniors 62 and over pay $2. A train and carousel cost $3 a ride.

places.name: Saddle River County Park
places.note: A path of about 6 miles runs along the Saddle River from Ridgewood to Rochelle Park. The Dunkerhook area in Paramus has a picnic pavilion and a waterfall.

sources: Bergen County Division of Senior Services

name: Ridgewood
intro: Ridgewood runs its senior programs out of Village Hall on North Maple Avenue, home to the Patrick A. Mancuso Senior Center. The HILT club welcomes residents 55 and over for monthly meetings and trips, a village senior bus runs three days a week, and residents 65 and over can buy half price taxi coupons.

seniorCenter.name: Patrick A. Mancuso Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: Part of the Community Center on the lowest level of Village Hall. The Community Center is being renovated, so some classes have moved elsewhere in Village Hall and the Stable. The HILT (Highlights in Leisure Time) Senior Club is open to village residents 55 and over for $25 a year, with monthly meetings at 10 a.m. and trips, usually on Thursdays (contact 201-670-5560).

transport.name: Village of Ridgewood Senior Bus
transport.notes: Call extension 2203 to book. Tuesdays the bus runs within Ridgewood, 9:30 a.m. to 2 p.m. On the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays it goes to Wyckoff ShopRite, and on 3rd Wednesdays to Ridgewood and nearby towns. Thursdays it serves towns next to Ridgewood. Schedules can change, so confirm when you call.

library.name: Ridgewood Public Library
library.notes: Offers eBooks, audiobooks, streaming films and online courses. Questions can go to ask@ridgewoodlibrary.org.

more.name: Senior Taxi Discount Coupons
more.note: Residents 65 and over can buy coupon books at the Village Hall lobby desk for about half the face value. Only Village Taxi (201-494-4444) accepts them, for local trips.

more.name: Age Friendly Ridgewood
more.note: Local initiative linked from the village website, with guides to housing, transportation, health and community activities.

more.name: Bergen County Division of Senior Services
more.note: The county helpline for information, care management, Medicare counseling (SHIP) and meals. Toll free 1-877-222-3737.

places.name: Wild Duck Pond
places.note: Part of Saddle River County Park, reached by car from East Ridgewood Avenue. Picnic areas, a pavilion and fishing with a state license.

places.name: Saddle River County Park path
places.note: A paved bike and walking path of about 6 miles that starts in Ridgewood and follows the Ho-Ho-Kus Brook and Saddle River south.

sources: Bergen County Division of Senior Services

name: Teaneck
intro: Teaneck's senior center fills the upper level of the Richard Rodda Community Center on Colonial Court and is open to adults 55 and up on weekdays. A public health nurse is there daily for blood pressure checks, and the township's parks include walking paths at Votee Park and trails in Overpeck County Park.

seniorCenter.name: Teaneck Senior Center, Richard Rodda Community Center
seniorCenter.notes: On the upper level. For adults 55 and up, Monday to Friday 9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed municipal holidays. Classes in education, fitness and social recreation, a game room with billiards and table tennis, and a public health nurse daily. Also reachable at 201-837-7130.

transport.name: Bergen County Division of Community Transportation
transport.notes: Teaneck's senior program page notes that a county van can bring participants to and from the center; ask the senior center office about it. Rides for seniors, frail residents and people with disabilities who live in Bergen County, for trips such as routine medical visits, physical therapy, shopping and senior activity centers. Call and press 1 for dispatch.

library.name: Teaneck Public Library
library.notes: Museum passes for Teaneck residents, eBooks and streaming on Hoopla and Kanopy, and Mango Languages.

more.name: Bergen County Division of Senior Services
more.note: The county helpline for information, care management, Medicare counseling (SHIP) and meals. Toll free 1-877-222-3737.

places.name: Overpeck County Park
places.note: About 805 acres around Overpeck Creek shared with four neighboring towns, with about five miles of trails, picnic and fishing spots and an outdoor amphitheater.

places.name: Milton A. Votee Park
places.note: Walking and bike paths, exercise stations and the Votee Park Rotary Band Shell.

places.name: Teaneck Creek Conservancy
places.note: A natural area with walking paths.

name: Fort Lee
intro: Fort Lee has its own Senior Services and Human Services department on Main Street, open weekdays with a program manager and activities coordinator on staff. The public library, also on Main Street, runs free AARP Senior Planet classes, and Fort Lee Historic Park offers river and bridge views from the top of the Palisades.

seniorCenter.name: Fort Lee Senior Services and Human Services
seniorCenter.notes: Ask for extension 1300. Office hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Call to ask about current senior activities and services.

transport.name: Bergen County Division of Community Transportation
transport.notes: Rides for seniors, frail residents and people with disabilities who live in Bergen County, for trips such as routine medical visits, physical therapy, shopping and senior activity centers. Call and press 1 for dispatch.

library.name: Fort Lee Public Library
library.notes: Hosts free AARP Senior Planet sessions on technology topics. Some sessions are for Fort Lee card holders only.

more.name: Jack Alter Fort Lee Community Center
more.note: 1355 Inwood Terrace. Seasonal classes have included chair yoga and stretch and tone.

more.name: Bergen County Division of Senior Services
more.note: The county helpline for information, care management, Medicare counseling (SHIP) and meals. Toll free 1-877-222-3737.

places.name: Fort Lee Historic Park
places.note: 33 acres atop the Palisades just south of the George Washington Bridge, with Hudson River and Manhattan views. The visitor center is open Wednesday to Sunday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.

places.name: Jack Alter Fort Lee Community Center
places.note: The borough's community center on Inwood Terrace, with seasonal classes and events.

name: Fair Lawn
intro: Fair Lawn's senior center on Gardiner Road is open to anyone 60 and over and serves a hot weekday lunch for a suggested $1.25. The borough minibus gives free rides anywhere in town, four senior social clubs meet regularly, and Saddle River County Park runs right through Fair Lawn.

seniorCenter.name: Fair Lawn Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: At the corner of 11th Street and Gardiner Road, one block from the library and Borough Hall. Open Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Saturday 10:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. and Sunday noon to 3 p.m.; closed borough holidays. For adults 60 and over, and family and caregivers are welcome. Lunch is served weekdays at noon for a suggested $1.25 donation; reserve at least 24 hours ahead.

transport.name: Fair Lawn Mini Bus
transport.notes: Free for Fair Lawn residents 18 and older, for trips within Fair Lawn. Weekdays except borough holidays, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Call up to two weeks ahead and by 3 p.m. the business day before. Your ride is not confirmed until staff call you back.

library.name: Maurice M. Pine Free Public Library
library.address: 10-01 Fair Lawn Avenue, Fair Lawn, NJ 07410
library.notes: Book clubs, museum passes, a digital library and hidden disability lanyards.

more.name: Fair Lawn senior social clubs
more.note: Fair Lawn has four senior social clubs, including the Friday Social Club and Happy Seniors Club. Meeting dates are on the senior center's monthly calendar.

more.name: Bergen County Division of Senior Services
more.note: The county helpline for information, care management, Medicare counseling (SHIP) and meals. Toll free 1-877-222-3737.

places.name: Fair Lawn Arboretum and Bird Sanctuary
places.note: A quiet green space on Fair Lawn Avenue between Radburn Road and Well Drive.

places.name: Garretson Forge and Farm
places.note: A preserved Revolutionary era homestead with seasonal tours and demonstrations.

places.name: Fair Lawn Community Theater
places.note: Plays, concerts and cultural events in the Fair Lawn Community Center.

places.name: Saddle River County Park
places.note: A long greenway with paths for walking, biking and picnics that runs through Fair Lawn.

name: Englewood
intro: In Englewood, the Southeast Senior Center for Independent Living, run by Bergen Family Center, offers free membership to anyone 57 and older, with exercise, language classes, a knitting group and a singing group. The city's health department runs public health nursing, and Flat Rock Brook Nature Center has 3.6 miles of trails.

seniorCenter.name: Southeast Senior Center for Independent Living (SESCIL)
seniorCenter.notes: Run by Bergen Family Center (44 Armory Street, Englewood); the phone is the agency's main line. Free membership for everyone 57 and older. Classes include aerobics, stretch and flex, yoga, tai chi, Italian, Spanish and French, plus a knitting group, the SESCIL Singers and support groups. Call for the center's location and hours.

transport.name: Bergen County Division of Community Transportation
transport.notes: Rides for seniors, frail residents and people with disabilities who live in Bergen County, for trips such as routine medical visits, physical therapy, shopping and senior activity centers. Call and press 1 for dispatch.

library.name: Englewood Public Library
library.notes: Computers and Wi-Fi, museum passes and eBook downloads.

more.name: Englewood Health Department, Public Health Nursing
more.note: 73 S Van Brunt Street. For the adult vaccination clinic, ask for the public health nurse at extension 511.

more.name: Bergen County Division of Senior Services
more.note: The county helpline for information, care management, Medicare counseling (SHIP) and meals. Toll free 1-877-222-3737.

places.name: Flat Rock Brook Nature Center
places.note: A 150 acre preserve at 443 Van Nostrand Avenue with 3.6 miles of forest trails. Trails are open dawn to dusk.

places.name: Mackay Park
places.note: The city's 28.6 acre park on Englewood Avenue, home to the Parks and Recreation office.

places.name: Overpeck County Park
places.note: A large county park shared by Englewood and four other towns, with about five miles of trails.

sources: Bergen County Division of Senior Services

name: Wyckoff
intro: Wyckoff and Christian Health Care Center run a senior bus on Tuesdays and Thursdays for residents over 55 and people with disabilities, with stops at doctors, the library, shopping centers and the YMCA. The township is also known for gentle green spaces such as the McFaul Environmental Center and The Gardens of Wyckoff.

seniorCenter.name: Northwest Senior Activity Center
seniorCenter.notes: Wyckoff's township site does not list its own senior center. This is the closest Bergen County run senior activity center we could confirm, in Midland Park. Open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Call to ask about membership and lunch.

transport.name: Wyckoff Senior Busing Program
transport.notes: Run by the township with Christian Health Care Center for seniors over 55 and people with disabilities who can reach the bus on their own. Tuesdays and Thursdays, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., home pick up to Wyckoff doctors, the library, post office, Town Hall, the YMCA, banks and the Wyckoff, Boulder Run and Cedar Hill shopping centers. Book Tuesday rides by 6 p.m. the Thursday before, and Thursday rides by 6 p.m. that Monday. A wheelchair accessible vehicle is available.

library.name: Wyckoff Free Public Library
library.notes: Adult programs, Tech Tips, notary service, museum passes, hotspot lending and a local history room.

more.name: Wyckoff Board of Health
more.note: Ask for extension 1000. Town Hall is at 340 Franklin Avenue.

more.name: Bergen County Division of Senior Services
more.note: The county helpline for information, care management, Medicare counseling (SHIP) and meals. Toll free 1-877-222-3737.

places.name: James A. McFaul Environmental Center
places.note: An 81 acre county park on Crescent Avenue with woodlands, gardens, a waterfowl pond and nature programs.

places.name: The Gardens of Wyckoff
places.note: A 12.8 acre sanctuary on Crescent Avenue with labeled plants, garden walkways, a pond and a brook.

places.name: Russell Farms Community Park
places.note: Five acres at 594 Russell Avenue with a trail, a gazebo, a butterfly garden and benches throughout.

sources: Bergen County Division of Senior Services

name: Mahwah
intro: Mahwah's Senior Activity Center on Corporate Drive serves people 62 and over on weekdays, with chair yoga, tai chi, watercolor, bridge and monthly health screenings. The township's Access Transportation offers curb to curb rides for a $1 suggested donation, and the area has big county parks like Darlington and Ramapo Valley.

seniorCenter.name: Mahwah Senior Activity Center
seniorCenter.notes: Township main line; the director is at extension 213. Open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., for people 62 and over. Programs include chair yoga, tai chi chih, Zumba Gold, Pilates, balance and fall prevention, watercolor, knitting, bridge, mahjong, line dancing, a monthly health screening, lectures, trips and special occasion luncheons.

transport.name: Mahwah Access Transportation
transport.notes: Curb to curb rides for Mahwah seniors, people with disabilities and residents who cannot drive. Trips go to doctors, PT and OT, and the senior center, and may include shopping centers, banks and the Midland Park Senior Activity Center. Call Access Transportation to join and to request rides. A $1 round trip donation is recommended.

library.name: Mahwah Public Library
library.notes: Offers home delivery (ask whether you qualify), public computers, adult events and a Tuesday morning yoga program.

more.name: Bergen County Division of Senior Services
more.note: The county helpline for information, care management, Medicare counseling (SHIP) and meals. Toll free 1-877-222-3737.

places.name: Darlington County Park
places.note: A 127 acre Bergen County park with walking paths, a summer swimming lake and lookout points over the water.

places.name: Continental Soldier's Park
places.note: At 550 Ramapo Valley Road, with a mulch path and bridges around Lake Henry, a gazebo and a covered picnic area.

places.name: Winter Park
places.note: On East Ramapo Avenue, with a pond, gazebo, picnic tables and a historic barn.

name: Ramsey
intro: Ramsey's senior center on East Oak Street is free to join for anyone 60 or older who lives in Ramsey or owns property there. Members get a monthly newsletter and a busy calendar of fitness, games and health screenings. The library offers homebound delivery, memory kits and dementia friendly services, and a borough van provides rides.

seniorCenter.name: Ramsey Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: Choose option 1. Open 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. No membership fee for anyone 60 or older who lives in or owns property in Ramsey. Activities include chair yoga, qi gong, Zumba Gold, a walking group, table tennis, bocce, shuffleboard, bingo, mahjong, canasta, knitting, a monthly book discussion and health screenings. Email seniors@ramseynj.com.

transport.name: Ramsey Van Transportation
transport.notes: Ask for extension 277. Listed in the Ramsey Senior Center newsletter. Call to ask who can ride, where it goes and how to book.

library.name: Ramsey Free Public Library
library.notes: Free homebound service by mail, dementia friendly services and memory kits, and tech assistance appointments.

places.name: Finch Park
places.note: On Church Street, with a pavilion and refreshment stand, restrooms, the VFW post and the Ramsey 9/11 memorial.

places.name: Darlington County Park
places.note: A 127 acre Bergen County park in neighboring Mahwah with walking paths and a summer swimming lake.

name: Morristown
intro: The Morristown Senior Center on South Street helps town residents with grocery trips, medical rides, benefits referrals, exercise classes and day trips, and mails a newsletter on request. The town's free Colonial Coach bus loops through Morristown, and Washington's Headquarters Museum is in town on Washington Place.

seniorCenter.name: Morristown Senior Center
seniorCenter.notes: Open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., for Town of Morristown residents. Services include grocery shopping help, medical transportation, benefits counseling referral, nutrition programs, day trips, the Sixty-Plus Club, exercise classes, AARP driver safety and tax preparation, and an aging in place home repair program.

transport.name: Morristown Senior Center van
transport.notes: Grocery pick up at 8 a.m. for about an hour of shopping: ShopRite on Tuesdays and Thursdays, Walmart on Wednesdays. Three bag limit. Reservations required. Ask the same number about medical transportation.

library.name: Morristown and Morris Township Library
library.notes: Free tech help Tuesday to Thursday, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., in 30 minute sessions for computers, smartphones, tablets and Kindles. There is also a bookmobile.

more.name: Colonial Coach
more.note: Free town bus for Morristown residents on one route in and around town, Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays (check the posted schedule for any Saturday service). The schedule is posted on the town site.

more.name: Wetmore Towers lunch site
more.note: Morris County midday meal for seniors, Monday to Friday. Free, with a $2 suggested donation. Call to register.

more.name: MAPS (Morris Area Paratransit System)
more.note: County paratransit for residents 60 and over, people with disabilities and veterans. Apply first. Suggested donation $1 per round trip.

more.name: Morris County Division of Aging, Disabilities and Community Programming
more.note: Information, referrals and help for older adults and caregivers, including care management and the county nutrition program. Toll free 800-564-4656.

places.name: Washington's Headquarters Museum
places.note: 30 Washington Place, part of Morristown National Historical Park. Open Thursday to Monday, 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Free guided Ford Mansion tours start here.

places.name: Jockey Hollow
places.note: Park grounds with a visitor center open Thursday to Monday, 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Grounds open daily from sunrise.

sources: Morris County Aging, Disabilities and Community Programming

name: Parsippany-Troy Hills
intro: Parsippany's Office on Aging works out of the Community Center on Knoll Road, with a weekday county lunch site, exercise classes, Medicare counseling and loaner wheelchairs and walkers. Seniors without a ride can book medical trips a week ahead, and the township runs two free buses for all residents from Morris Hills Shopping Center.

seniorCenter.name: Parsippany Community Center and Office on Aging
seniorCenter.notes: Also 973-263-7352. Recreation and socializing weekdays, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Senior exercise classes (call for fees), a county lunch site (reserve a day ahead at 973-884-1868), SHIP Medicare counseling by appointment, help with benefit forms, loaner wheelchairs, walkers and canes, and free AARP tax help starting each February.

transport.name: Parsippany Office on Aging medical transportation
transport.notes: For Parsippany seniors who have no other ride or family to drive them. Riders must be ambulatory. Rides go to local doctors and supermarkets. Call at least one week ahead; medical appointments get top priority.

library.name: Parsippany-Troy Hills Public Library
library.notes: Main library of the township system. There are also branches in Lake Hiawatha (68 Nokomis Avenue) and Mount Tabor (31 Trinity Park).

more.name: Parsippany-Troy Hills Free Transit System
more.note: Free for Parsippany residents, no reservation. Two routes start at Morris Hills Shopping Center and run on the hour on weekdays.

more.name: Parsippany Health Department clinics
more.note: Health clinics, including screenings, through the year. Call for dates.

more.name: Skylands RSVP Friendly Visitor and Telephone Reassurance
more.note: Ask about Friendship at Heart. Free weekly visits or daily check in calls from volunteers.

more.name: Morris County Division of Aging, Disabilities and Community Programming
more.note: Information, referrals and help for older adults and caregivers, including care management and the county nutrition program. Toll free 800-564-4656.

places.note: A 420 acre county park with over 11 miles of paved and natural trails, open daily sunrise to sunset.

places.name: Craftsman Farms
places.note: A 30 acre historic site that was once the home of furniture designer Gustav Stickley.

places.note: On Lake Shore Drive, with a gazebo honoring two residents who died in the Vietnam War.

name: Madison
intro: Madison shares a senior center with the Chathams through a shared service agreement, so residents can use the Senior Center of the Chathams on Meyersville Road. At home, the borough's senior transportation program offers same day custom rides around town plus regular trips to ShopRite, Stop and Shop and Walmart.

seniorCenter.name: Senior Center of the Chathams
seniorCenter.notes: Madison has a shared service agreement with this center, which offers social, recreational, educational and wellness programs to Madison residents. Open Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. Email info@chathamseniorcenter.org.

transport.name: Madison Senior Transportation
transport.notes: Choose option 1. For Madison residents 18 and older, to any Madison location and ShopRite of Chatham. Custom rides Monday, Wednesday and Friday, 9 a.m. to noon; set grocery runs Tuesday and Thursday; Walmart on the 2nd and 4th Thursdays. Same day reservations open at 8 a.m. Schedule subject to change.

library.name: Madison Public Library
library.notes: Tech Help sessions, chair yoga, a knitting group, book discussions and an adult movie matinee.

more.name: Madison Senior Services
more.note: Borough page with senior transportation and a Meals on Wheels flyer. The phone is the borough's senior transportation line. Hartley Dodge Memorial Building, 50 Kings Road.

more.name: Morris County Nutrition Program, home delivered meals
more.note: Meals for homebound seniors who qualify. Call for an assessment.

more.name: Morris County Division of Aging, Disabilities and Community Programming
more.note: Information, referrals and help for older adults and caregivers, including care management and the county nutrition program. Toll free 800-564-4656.

places.name: Madison Community Arts Center
places.note: 10 Kings Road, a five minute walk from the train station, with film festivals, art shows and theater. Free street and nearby parking.

places.name: Madison Public Library
places.note: Regular chair yoga, knitting and movie matinees on Keep Street.

name: Chatham (Borough)
intro: Chatham Borough residents use the Senior Center of the Chathams on Meyersville Road for wellness classes, lifelong learning, support groups and caregiver advice. The Library of the Chathams on Main Street delivers books to homebound residents, and the borough's Health and Social Services office on Fairmount Avenue can point you to county help.

seniorCenter.name: Senior Center of the Chathams
seniorCenter.notes: Listed by the borough as its senior center. Open Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. Programs cover wellness and fitness, enrichment classes and lectures, support and connection groups, and information and referral for seniors and caregivers.

transport.name: MAPS (Morris Area Paratransit System)
transport.notes: Chatham does not appear on the county's list of municipal Dial a Ride programs, so MAPS is the main option. Apply first with proof of eligibility. Suggested donation $1 per round trip.

library.name: Library of the Chathams
library.notes: Home delivery for Chatham residents who are homebound or cannot get to the library for health reasons. Staff and Friends volunteers bring books and movies to your door, usually within a day or two.

more.name: Chatham Borough Health and Social Services
more.note: 54 Fairmount Avenue. Open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

more.name: Morris County Nutrition Program, home delivered meals

places.note: Off Parrott Mill Road, with a walking trail, a sheltered picnic area and a boat launch.

places.name: Garden Park

name: Randolph
intro: Randolph runs senior programs from the Township Community Center on Calais Road, right next to the library, with day trips, outings, movie nights and card games. Residents 60 and over can get a $10 Senior ID card for free swimming at Randolph Lake, and the township Dial-A-Ride covers medical visits and Monday shopping.

seniorCenter.name: Randolph Township Community Center
seniorCenter.notes: Senior programs through the Community Services Department include "Just For the Fun of It" day trips, monthly outings, movie nights, cards and games. The Senior ID Card for residents 60 and over costs $10 a year and includes free admission to township sporting events, free swimming at Randolph Lake and free tennis at Brundage Park.

transport.notes: For permanent Randolph residents 60 and over, and disabled adults 18 and over who receive Social Security disability. Medical trips Monday to Thursday to doctors within 10 miles of Town Hall, for appointments between 9 a.m. and 3 p.m.; book as soon as you make the appointment. Shopping trips on Mondays to ShopRite or Walmart in Roxbury; book by Friday.
